glance.question: Is deconstruction apostasy, a needed reckoning, or a season to pastor through?

positions.name: Deconstruction as Apostasy
positions.claim: It starts with secondary doubts and slides toward denying core Christian truths.

positions.name: Deconstruction as Necessary Reckoning
positions.claim: Testing an inherited, sometimes harmful faith can end in a more honest, owned faith.

positions.name: Pastoring Through Deconstruction
positions.claim: Churches can hold to doctrine and still walk patiently with people who doubt.

start_here.title: Doubt, Deconstruction, and Patient Faith
start_here.author: Jay Y. Kim
start_here.why: Kim, who went through doubt, deconstruction and deconversion in college, makes the case for patience.

start_here.title: Editor’s Note: Defending Sound Doctrine Against the Deconstruction of American Evangelicalism
start_here.author: Jonathan Leeman
start_here.why: An argument that limited interpreters can still know and guard sound doctrine.

start_here.title: Help Stop Deconstruction. Become a Non-Anxious Presence.
start_here.author: Andrew Kelley
start_here.why: How friends and pastors can stay close to someone in a crisis of faith without rushing to win the argument.

key_number.text: Of young adults who attended a Protestant church regularly as teens, 66% dropped out for at least a year between ages 18 and 22; 31% of those dropouts now attend twice a month or more.
key_number.study: Most Teenagers Drop Out of Church When They Become Young Adults
